literature_notes: All six ledger clips (L1–L6) describe C-terminal fusions on full-length ABCB11/BSEP: L1 and L2 report a GSGS-HiBiT tag appended after the last residue; L3 and L4 report C-terminal GFP; L5 and L6 describe EGFP- or GFP-tagged constructs that traffic to the canalicular membrane, referencing the same C-terminal GFP construct established in L3/L4. The C-terminus (position 1321, residue S) lies within the intracellular domain (landmarks: 1039–1321), 283 residues past the end of TM12 (1018–1038). A C-terminal tag on an intracellular terminus does not qualify as an extracellular surface tag site. No ledger clip describes a tag at the N-terminus, in any extracellular loop (EL1 83–144, EL2 238–242, EL3 344–359, EL4 775–799, EL5 897–901, EL6 1001–1017), or at any other extracellular position. The N-terminus (residues 1–58) is also intracellular. Because no ledger line supports an extracellular insertion, the correct answer is zero qualifying sites.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal GSGS-HiBiT tag appended after the last residue (S1321); the C-terminus lies in the intracellular domain (1039–1321), confirmed by topology landmarks; protein traffics correctly to the plasma membrane but the tag faces the cytoplasm.

C-terminal GFP fusion (wild-type and missense variants A257V, T463I, G562D) used in MDCK and hepatocellular expression studies; same intracellular C-terminal position as L1; canalicular surface display of the full-length protein is confirmed but the GFP moiety is intracellular.
